column1: # Hand-labelled ground truth for the zero-drift probe pair.
# Written by the person who wrote both sides of the port, so these are the *correct*
# migrations rather than statistically plausible ones. This is the regression target the
# corpus-mined rule set is scored against.
# gained = NONE       the symbol has no replacement; the capability was removed or absorbed
# gained = ARTIFACT   not a real migration. The symbol differs only because of how the port
#                     was written (a factory method instead of a constructor), not because
#                     anything changed in the API. Excluded from scoring.
# Where a single lost symbol legitimately has several valid targets, alternatives are
# separated by '|' and a prediction matching any of them counts as correct.
# --- removed outright: the capability moved to a different mechanism ---
# The mod event bus and ModContainer are injected into the mod constructor in NeoForge, so
# there is nothing to call. A transformer cannot rewrite these call sites; it has to rewrite
# the constructor signature. This is precisely the class of migration a symbol-to-symbol rule
# table cannot express, and it sits at the very top of the work list at 241 corpus mods.
# Subsumed: the registry key is now implied by createBlocks/createItems.
# --- artifacts of how the port was written, not API changes ---
